prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a finished wide 16:9 game background painting, high resolution, for the Shipyard II construction screen in Stellar Syndicates.
Primary request: a close-up INTERIOR view of the planetary Shipyard II where the player can clearly see a ship being built.
Input image 1 is the architecture, materials, palette, and rendering-style reference: the existing planetary Shipyard II exterior. Reconstruct a believable inside of THAT compact reinforced two-section assembly hangar. Input image 2 is the ship identity reference: the game's small industrial freighter, shown here completed; depict this same recognizable type only partway through construction. These are reference inputs, not images to paste into the scene.

Camera and framing: full-bleed immersive interior, landscape 16:9. The camera is inside the hangar near the entrance, from a slightly elevated three-quarter inspection viewpoint, looking diagonally across the central fabrication cradle. Close enough for the exposed ship structure and assembly tools to be clearly readable, with the whole unfinished ship visible. Strong coherent perspective and believable ground contact. Show the ceiling, substantial support columns, and rear service wall to establish an enclosed planetary industrial building, with a glimpse of the neighboring second work bay. Keep the foreground edge and outer corners relatively quiet for future game controls, without actually drawing interface elements.

Ship under construction: one small freighter roughly halfway assembled, resting on substantial mechanical supports along recessed parallel floor rails. Preserve its compact broad utility silhouette, small central cockpit, paired aft engine housings and modular side cargo bodies from reference image 2. Some ivory-gray hull plates are fitted; large open sections reveal the connected keel, ribs, internal structure and cabling. A yellow overhead gantry is positioning one unfinished panel just above an exposed section. Two restrained industrial assembly arms work beside the cradle, with one small precise welding glow. The incomplete state must be unmistakable, while the ship remains a clear cohesive focal object. No floating completed ship, no flying engines, no launch flames.

Architecture and mood: match the reference's weathered gray/slate steel, chunky pale structural frames, yellow crane equipment, amber work lamps, inset cyan service indicators, heavy braced columns, overhead beams, ventilation pipes, wall cabinets, floor grates, and restrained black-yellow safety markings. This is a useful compact Tier II fabrication hall, not a cathedral-sized space station. Layered cool ambient illumination and warm practical lamps, enough soft task light to see the ship's open structure. Atmospheric but readable shadows, restrained highlights and minimal haze.

Style: polished semi-realistic science-fiction game environment art, physically convincing industrial geometry, gently painterly material finish consistent with Shipyard II, carefully composed large forms and selective fine detail. No cartoon outline, no plastic toy look.
Constraints: single scene, no labels, no words, no numbers, no signage text, no logos, no watermark, no UI, no progress bars, no people, no windows showing outer space, no starfield, no planet vista, no explosions, no giant foreground objects hiding the ship. Opaque background.
